p: commend unto you Phebe our sister: Having made an end of the whole discussion, he comes now to familiar commendations and salutations, and that to good consideration and purpose, that is, that the Romans might know who are most to be honoured and to be considered among them: and also whom they ought to set before them to follow: and therefore he attributes to every of them individual and singular testimonies.
Lord: For Christ's sake, which appropriately belongs to the Christians, for the heathen philosophers have a resemblance of the same virtues.
church that is in their house: The company of the faithful, for in so great a city as that was, there were different companies.
firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ: For he was the first of Achaia that believed in Christ: and this type of speech is an allusion to the ceremonies of the law.
Christ before me: Ingrafted by faith.
kiss: He calls that a holy kiss which proceeds from a heart that is full of that holy love: now this is to be understood as referring to the manner used in those days.

Now I beseech you: As by describing by name those who were worthy of commendation he sufficiently declared whom they ought to hear and follow, so does he now point out to them whom they ought to take heed of, yet he does not name them, because it was not necessary.
mark them which cause divisions and: Watchfully and diligently, as though you should scout for your enemies in a watch tower.

good words and fair speeches deceive: The word which he uses signifies a promising which accomplishes nothing, and if you hear any such, you may assure yourself that he who promises to you is more concerned about receiving from you than he is concerned about giving to you.
For your obedience is come abroad: Simplicity must be joined with wisdom.

wise unto that which is good: Furnished with the knowledge of the truth and wisdom, so that you may embrace good things, and avoid evil, beware of the deceits and snares of false prophets, and resist them openly: and this place plainly destroys the papists faith of credit, whereas they maintain it to be sufficient for one man to believe as another man believes, without further knowledge or examination what the matter is, or what ground it has: using these daily speeches, "We believe as our fathers believed, and we believe as the Church believes."
simple concerning evil: As men that know no way to deceive, much less deceive indeed.
And the God of peace shall: We must fight with a certain hope of victory.

Timotheus my workfellow: He adds salutations, partly to renew mutual friendship, and partly to the end that this epistle might be of some weight with the Romans, having the confirmation of so many that subscribed to it.
wrote this epistle: Wrote it as Paul uttered it.
The grace of our Lord Jesus: Now taking his leave of them this third time, he wishes that to them, upon which all the force of the former doctrine depends.

Now to him that is of: He sets forth the power and wisdom of God with great thanksgiving, which especially appears in the gospel, and makes mention also of the calling of the Gentiles, to confirm the Romans in the hope of this salvation.
mystery: That secret and hidden thing, that is to say, the calling of the Gentiles.
made known to all nations for: Offered and exhibited to all nations to be known.
